subject: Retention & BYOK: audit log jurisdiction mapping and SSO evidence
messages:
From: Tua Laine <security@helsinkihealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Retention & BYOK: audit log jurisdiction mapping and SSO evidence

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist we need to validate two things before we can sign the PO: a) how Redwood maps audit-log retention by EU member-state jurisdiction (we have processing locations in Finland, Sweden, and Germany) and b) confirmation of BYOK/KMS workflow for keys that must remain under our control.

We also need a clear list of SSO audit events we can export (login, token issuance, identity provider metadata changes, SCIM provisioning events) and whether those exports include IP / region tags and timestamps in UTC. Our legal/privacy team is insisting on a per-country retention table and any data residency guarantees you can provide.

Attached is a short evidence checklist (evidence_requirements.pdf) — can you triage what we can provide from hosted vs. private deployments and an estimated timeline for any product work required? If possible, please split answers into: immediate evidence we can provide, configuration steps for Dedicated, and gaps that would require new dev work.

Best,

Tua Laine
Head of Security Operations
Helsinki Health

----
Attachment: evidence_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tua Laine <security@helsinkihealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Retention & BYOK: audit log jurisdiction mapping and SSO evidence

Hi Tua — thanks for the clear checklist and for outlining the three buckets; that makes triage easier. I’ve looped in Marissa (product) and Grace (Security/Compliance) to help scope the work and call out what’s already available. Quick notes now so you have visibility:

- Hosted (Redwood API): we provide audit logs at the tenant level with UTC timestamps, event types, and IP addresses. Current hosted retention is configurable by plan up to 365 days; per-country retention by default is not provided today.
- Dedicated / Private: we can surface raw audit streams or S3 delivery for dedicated customers; BYOK support exists in our Private offering via customer-managed KMS but there are a few integration edge-cases to call out (key rotation semantics and escrow for disaster recovery).
- SSO events: we emit common events (login, logout, token issuance, metadata change). SCIM provisioning events are available for Dedicated.

I’ll ask the team to produce: (1) a per-jurisdiction mapping doc marking "supported today" / "configurable" / "would require product work", (2) a short BYOK workflow diagram + gaps, and (3) an export sample (sanitized) showing fields (timestamp, ip, event_type, idp, country_tag).

Can Marissa/Grace confirm availability for a 30-min working session tomorrow to align on scope and timelines? Tua — what timezone works best?

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

> As part of our procurement checklist we need to validate two things before we can sign the PO: a) how Redwood maps audit-log retention by EU member-state jurisdiction (we have processing locations in Finland, Sweden, and Germany) and b) confirmation of BYOK/KMS workflow for keys that must remain under our control.
>

- Me: I’ll draft the BYOK workflow and note gaps for disaster recovery (escrow), rotation, and consent flows. I’ve started a short draft file (byok-design-notes.md) and will attach once I have the initial version.

We should aim to respond to Tua with a consolidated packet within 24–36 hours if possible; if product gaps are larger we’ll call those out with a roadmap ETA. Thoughts?

Thanks — Priyom

Thanks Priyom — quick triage and next steps below. I’ve attached a working draft for the jurisdiction matrix and a note on product gaps.

Summary (high level):
- Immediate evidence (we can provide within 24 hours): hosted audit export sample (sanitized CSV), list of SSO event types with field-level schema, hosted retention policy doc. See attached: evidence_requirements.pdf (trimmed) and the matrix draft.
- Dedicated / Private: supported today via S3 delivery of raw logs and customer-managed KMS. We need to document the steps for configuring per-country retention buckets — operational playbook is available but not yet a self-serve UI.
- Product gaps (require roadmap items): per-tenant per-country retention enforcement for Hosted (ETA: Q4 2027 scoping; depends on infra tagging work), automated key-escrow workflow for BYOK (security review scheduled; ETA: Q1 2028 if prioritized).

Action items:
1) Priyom — finalize the BYOK workflow diagram and capture rotation/escrow exceptions (I’ll add to the roadmap note).
2) Grace — sanitize and attach the hosted audit export sample (CSV) and confirm IP/country tag fields.
3) Priyom/Grace/Marissa — 30-min sync tomorrow 09:00 UTC to finalize the packet for Tua.

Attaching: byok-design-notes.md (draft), jurisdiction-matrix-v1.csv

If Tua is okay with the packet, we can move to an NDA-lined evidence exchange and then plan a 1-week pilot on Dedicated with S3 log delivery for their security team to validate.
